  • Board members provided brief introductions, followed by a BINGO
  icebreaker activity.

2.  25-56158  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation from the City Attorney’s Office
  on the Brown Act and Robert's Rules of Order.

  A motion was made by Member Lock, seconded by Member Scott, to approve
  recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Diles III, Boyce, Wee, Topolewski, Tan, Shuford, Scott, McFadzen,
  Martins, Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Rockenbach, Lowery-Luyties

  • City Attorney Nicholas Masero delivered a presentation on the Brown Act
  and Robert’s Rules. Key points highlighted included that board meetings
  must be open to the public and can only occur when a majority of
  commission members are present simultaneously at the same location.
  Additionally, serial communication among members is prohibited, and all
  meeting agenda items must be posted at least 72 hours in advance of the
  meeting.

3.  25-56213  Recommendation to discuss recruitment of new members for the Long Beach
  Continuum of Care Board and its subcommittees.

  A motion was made by Member Brezenoff, seconded by Member Martins, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Diles III, Boyce, Wee, Topolewski, Tan, Shuford, Scott, McFadzen,
  Martins, Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Rockenbach, Lowery-Luyties

  • Health Department staff member Jeffrey Proctor provided updates on the
  Long Beach CoC Board, including open seats, membership requirements,
  upcoming general membership meetings, and subcommittee meetings. The
  Board discussed the eligibility criteria for new members, and staff will follow

  up by sending an email with application details to interested parties.

4.  25-56214  Recommendation to receive and file the ICF International, Inc. and Los Angeles
  Homeless Services Authority (LAHSA) governance presentation regarding the
  Coordinated Entry System (CES) policy and the Los Angeles Homeless
  Management Information System (LA HMIS) collaboration.

  A motion was made by Member Rockenbach, seconded by Member
  McFadzen, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  14 Diles III, Boyce, Wee, Topolewski, Tan, Shuford, Scott, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 1 Lowery-Luyties

  • Kimberly Farnham and Jessica Reed from LAHSA attended the meeting in
  person to present on CES and HMIS. They provided an overview of the CoC,
  including its purpose and governance structure. The Board’s role in
  overseeing HMIS and CES policies was discussed, with clarification that all
  four CoCs are utilizing the same HMIS implementation. In addition, the
  governance and policy timeline was reviewed, covering the years 2017
  through 2024.
  • Proposed LA HMIS Collaborative: Policy/advisory body with equal standing
  across CoCs. Decisions affecting all CoCs made collaboratively; local issues
  decided locally. Scope includes HMIS P&Ps, privacy/security standards, data
  use agreements, vendor/software evaluation.
  • Next steps include fall 2025, draft membership and charter updates,;
  Nov./December 2025, CoC General Membership votes on governance
  charter changes, and Jan/Feb 2026, outreach and seating of the HMIS
  collaborative.
  • Board members, staff, and LAHSA representatives engaged in a discussion
  to address additional questions raised by the board for clarification.

5.  25-56430  Recommendation to review and submit feedback to staff regarding Request for
  Proposal (RFP) HSB-2026-002 “Continuum of Care Portfolio”.

  A motion was made by Member Lock, seconded by Member Martins, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  14 Diles III, Boyce, Wee, Topolewski, Tan, Shuford, Scott, Rockenbach,

  Page 3 of 7

  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 10:00 AM

  McFadzen, Martins, Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff, Amick
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 1  Lowery-Luyties

  • Health Department staff Jeffrey Proctor presented to the board regarding the
  NOFO, originally intended as a two-year award that would not require
  reapplication this year. However, there are plans to release a new NOFO this
  year, with no set date announced. Staff are preparing the RFP and
  requested the board’s input and recommendations. Due to time constraints,
  the RFP will not accept new project proposals at this time.
  • Staff and board members also discussed ranking and scoring.

6.  25-56215  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on proposed updates to the
  Long Beach Continuum of Care Charter and Bylaws.

  A motion was made by Member McFadzen, seconded by Member Brown-
  Shock, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  14 Diles III, Boyce, Wee, Topolewski, Tan, Shuford, Scott, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Lock, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 1 Lowery-Luyties

  • Health Department staff member Jeffrey Proctor presented updates to the
  Charter and Bylaws, which included certification of prior amendments,
  adjustments to meeting schedules, updates to department naming, and
  alignment with written standards and Board-approved policies.
  • The next steps include Board review and formal approval of the proposed
  Charter and Bylaws updates.

7.  25-56216  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on the Data and Quality Plan.

  A motion was made by Member Martins, seconded by Member McFadzen, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  13 Diles III, Boyce, Wee, Topolewski, Tan, Shuford, Scott, Rockenbach,
  McFadzen, Martins, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff, Amick
  No:  0 None

  Page 4 of 7

  TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 9, 2025
  1500 HUGHES WAY STE. C-300 LONG BEACH, CA 90810
  HOUSING AUTHORITY, 10:00 AM

  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 2 Lowery-Luyties, Lock

  • Health Department staff Paul Duncan provided an overview. System
  performance measures are a crucial part of systems management because
  they help monitor, analyze, and improve system’s efficiency and
  effectiveness.
  • standard deviation is used to determine statistical difference positive or
  negative in comparison to a group of like measurements.
  • There have been ways to respond to how performance is looked at including
  improved ways of differentiating performance across the portfolio of
  agencies.
  • a recap of the System Performance Measures implemented two years ago
  was also discussed.
  • Members of the board raised questions concerning the HMIS merge and
  sought clarification on how SCAN data will be protected throughout the
  process.

8.  25-56217  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation approving the Ranking and
  Prioritization Policy and Methodology.

  A motion was made by Member Rockenbach, seconded by Member Shuford,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Diles III, Boyce, Wee, Shuford, Scott, Rockenbach, McFadzen,
  Martins, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Topolewski, Tan, Lowery-Luyties, Lock

  • Paul Duncan, Health Department staff, provided an overview of the Long
  Beach CoC ranking and prioritization policies. He explained that agencies
  will be evaluated based on their performance across key categories,
  including project outcomes and fiscal management.
  • For Transitional Housing–Rapid Rehousing (TH-RRH) programs, scoring will
  be applied in the category where the majority of the program’s budget is
  concentrated. Performance data will be drawn from the Homeless
  Management Information System (HMIS) or other comparable databases to
  ensure consistency and reliability.
  • Additional performance measures will be introduced to strengthen the
  system’s ability to track, evaluate, and report outcomes comprehensively.

  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Topolewski, Tan, Lowery-Luyties, Lock

  • The board moved to bring this item back for consideration at the next
  meeting, as staff continue finalizing the Reallocation Policy and
  Methodology.
  • Members Tan and Topolewski departed the meeting.

10. 25-56219  Recommendation to conduct a discussion on the Long Beach Continuum of Care
  Strategic Plan Updates.

  A motion was made by Member Shuford, seconded by Member Rockenbach,
  to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  11 Diles III, Boyce, Wee, Shuford, Scott, Rockenbach, McFadzen,
  Martins, Brown-Shock, Brezenoff, Amick
  No:  0 None
  Recused: 0 None
  Abstain: 0 None
  Absent: 4 Topolewski, Tan, Lowery-Luyties, Lock

  • Health Department staff Jeffrey Proctor provided updates on the Strategic
  Plan established in 2023 and sought input from the board on whether to
  continue with the current strategies. The discussion addressed delegation of
  these strategies, including the role and responsibilities of subcommittees.
  • Members expressed concerns regarding subcommittee meeting times and
  schedules as outlined in the Strategic Plan. Staff also highlighted the option
  of convening ad hoc meetings, which can be called as needed and are not
  subject to Brown Act or Robert’s Rules requirements
